evals.prompt: We're rebranding our SaaS. We're thinking we want to feel more 'premium' — can you help us define our brand strategy?
evals.expected_output: Should run the discovery session, not immediately generate outputs. Should detect 'premium' as marketing speak and fire the coaching trigger — push to 'premium like *what*? what does it feel like?' Should NOT hand over a finished brand strategy or a list of concept directions until the session is complete. Should ask one question at a time, coaching the answers before moving on.
assertions: Does not immediately generate brand strategy outputs or concept directions
Detects 'premium' as marketing speak and fires the coaching trigger
Asks one question at a time
Coaches before accepting shallow/marketing answers

evals.prompt: What muses should we use? We're a fintech.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT generate a list of muses for fintech without first establishing the emotional target. Should explain that muses come after the emotional target is clear — and offer to either start the discovery session, or (if a target is already defined) use it to find muses. Should not suggest 'Bloomberg Terminal, private banking, luxury watches' or any generic fintech muses without knowing what feeling this specific brand is after.
assertions: Does not generate fintech muse suggestions without an established emotional target
Explains the dependency (muses flow from the emotional target)
Offers to start discovery or use an existing target

evals.prompt: Just give us three concept directions for our rebrand. We don't want to do the whole discovery thing.
evals.expected_output: Should explain that concept directions without an emotional target are random — then offer a fast path: 3–4 questions instead of the full session to establish the emotional target, *then* generate directions. Should NOT immediately produce generic concept directions (e.g. 'Bold & Industrial / Warm & Human / Clean & Minimal') before any emotional target is known.
assertions: Does not produce generic concept directions without an emotional target
Offers a fast-path alternative (a few key questions)
Explains why directions without a target are arbitrary

evals.prompt: Our brand name is 'Magister.' We want to feel authoritative and trustworthy. Can you help define our brand strategy?
evals.expected_output: Should mine the name's etymology BEFORE the session begins: Magister = Latin for 'master,' 'supreme commander,' used as the Roman military title for 'Master of Soldiers' (the highest field rank). Should bring this as a provocation ('your name literally means the supreme commander of Roman legions — is there an identity in that imperial-command lineage?'). Should not ignore the name or treat it as a neutral label. Should then ask one discovery question at a time, coaching the answers.
assertions: Mines the name's etymology and brings it as a provocation before or during the session
Names the specific meaning (Latin for supreme commander / master) as a provocation
Does not ignore the name or treat it as a neutral label
Asks one question at a time and coaches

evals.prompt: I know what I want the brand to feel like — like Apollo Mission Control. Let's skip the questions and go straight to muses and concept directions.
evals.expected_output: Should treat Apollo Mission Control as a candidate muse, not an established target. Should fetch a real image of the Apollo Mission Control room BEFORE accepting it, show it, and ask 'which part of this is the feeling?' (the amber CRT glow? the graph-paper charts? the human density and urgency? the institutional green walls?). Should NOT skip to concept directions — it should record the cue at render fidelity, then use it to anchor the emotional target before generating directions.
assertions: Fetches and shows a real image of Apollo Mission Control before accepting it as a muse
Asks which specific visual element is the feeling (not just 'got it, moving on')
Records the cue at render fidelity (texture / material / light level), not as a label
Does not skip to concept directions before the emotional target is established

evals.prompt: Our ideal user is a 35-year-old SaaS founder who shops at Whole Foods and reads the WSJ. They want to feel 'in control.'
evals.expected_output: Should fire the 'capability not emotion' trigger on 'in control' — push to 'in control to feel *what*? calm? elite? confident?' Should fire the 'too generic' trigger on the user description — push for a *person*, not a demographic sketch. Should fire the coaching trigger if 'in control' is restated without getting to the underlying feeling. Should NOT accept 'in control' as the emotional target and move on.
assertions: Fires the capability-not-emotion trigger on 'in control'
Pushes past 'in control' to the underlying feeling (calm / elite / confident / etc.)
Flags the user description as too demographic and asks for a real person
Does not accept 'in control' as the emotional target

evals.prompt: We want the brand to feel warm, human, and approachable — like Airbnb but for enterprise software. Our muse is Airbnb.
evals.expected_output: Should fetch a real image of Airbnb's brand/marketing BEFORE accepting it as a muse. Should push on the *visual cue*: which part — the Lo-Fi illustration? the photography warmth? the Cereal typeface's friendliness? The muse isn't captured until the cue is recorded at render fidelity. Should flag the contradiction between 'warm/approachable' and 'enterprise' — not smooth it over — and ask which wins when they conflict. Should not accept 'Airbnb' as a muse without an image and a specific stealable cue.
assertions: Fetches a real Airbnb brand image before accepting the muse
Asks which specific visual cue is the feeling (illustration style / photo warmth / typeface / etc.)
Records the cue at render fidelity, not as 'warm like Airbnb'
Flags the warm/approachable vs. enterprise contradiction and asks which wins

evals.prompt: We've finished the discovery. Our emotional target is: 1. Capable authority. 2. Calm clarity. 3. Earned trust. Now generate three concept directions for our Revolution.
evals.expected_output: Should generate three genuinely distinct concept directions — each with a name, an emotional angle on the target (how each direction delivers 'capable authority + calm clarity + earned trust'), a visual world description, a muse board hint, and a 'what we'd steal' note. Directions should be substantially different from each other — not just three shades of the same aesthetic. Should NOT produce generic labels ('Bold & Confident / Warm & Human / Clean & Minimal') that don't connect to the specific emotional target.
assertions: Generates three substantially distinct directions (not three shades of the same aesthetic)
Each direction connects specifically to the emotional target (capable authority / calm clarity / earned trust)
Each direction includes a visual world description and a 'what we'd steal' cue
Does not produce generic direction labels disconnected from the emotional target
